title: Receivers
hints: The tests call r.Area() and r.Scale(2), which are methods. A method is declared with a receiver in parentheses before its name: func (r Rect) Area() float64.

A value receiver works on a copy, so Scale's changes vanish when it returns. A pointer receiver, func (r *Rect) Scale(...), changes the caller's Rect. Go takes &r for you when you call r.Scale on an addressable value.
func (r Rect) Area() float64 { return r.Width * r.Height } and func (r *Rect) Scale(f float64) { r.Width *= f; r.Height *= f }
